test_title: PYST 28: SSC MTS 2022 - Quantitative Aptitude(Held On: 16 May, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: 14 workers working 16 hours per day can demolish a building in 81 days. In how many days 18 workers working 24 hours per day can demolish the same building?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct MDH formula: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

⇒ 14 × 81 × 16 = 18 × D₂ × 24

⇒ D₂ = (14 × 81 × 16) ÷ (18 × 24)

⇒ D₂ = 18144 ÷ 432

⇒ D₂ = 42 days

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Workers in first group (M₁) = 14

Days taken (D₁) = 81

Hours per day (H₁) = 16

Workers in second group (M₂) = 18

Hours per day (H₂) = 24

**Formula Used:**

Since the building to be demolished is the same, the total work is constant (W₁ = W₂).

MDH Rule: M₁ × D₁ × H₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂

 
 Group 1
 14 M × 81 D × 16 H
 
 =
 
 
 Group 2
 18 M × D × 24 H

**Calculation:**

⇒ 14 × 81 × 16 = 18 × D₂ × 24

⇒ D₂ = (14 × 81 × 16) ÷ (18 × 24)

Simplifying the ratios step-by-step:

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (81 ÷ 18) × (16 ÷ 24)

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (9 ÷ 2) × (2 ÷ 3)

Canceling out the common factor of 2:

⇒ D₂ = 14 × (9 ÷ 3)

⇒ D₂ = 14 × 3

⇒ D₂ = 42 days

**∴ The correct answer is 42 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

The rule states that if M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours a day, and M₂ persons can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours a day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Work Equivalence Principle

When two groups perform the exact same task, the total effort measured in man-hours or man-days remains constant. Thus, Total Work = Men × Days × Hours.

Direct and Inverse Proportions

More work requires more workers (direct proportion, M ∝ W). More workers require fewer days to complete the same work (inverse proportion, M ∝ 1 ÷ D).
